To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified a set of 34 proteins and their 38 PPI interactions in the SSU processosome, and that we have shown that this set has a low coverage by the current HT-Y2H and PCA datasets.

we have identified a number of protein interactions between proteins in the SSU processosome that were previously unknown, and that we have found that the current high throughput datasets do not adequately capture the interactions of the SSU proccessome.
the SSU processomes are highly conserved in eukaryotes and that the protein-protein interaction network for the SSU processosome is largely unknown.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the assembly, architecture, and function of the eukaryotic small ribosomal sub-unit (SSU) pre-ribosomal particle, also referred to as the SSU processosome, a ribonucleoparticle (RNP) complex of 72 proteins and one small nucleolar RNA.
the assembly and architecture of a large ribonulceoprotein complex involved with ribosomal RNA processing and small ribosomal sub-unit biogenesis.
the identification of protein-protein interaction networks and their role in the assembly of ribosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SSU processosome is not a well characterized complex.
there are no genome-wide Y2-H studies for the SSU processosome, and thus the PPI network for the SSU-processosome is largely unknown.
the SSU processosome interactome is largely unexplored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SSU processomes from all organisms are highly conserved and the interactions among its components are highly conserved, but the interactions have been poorly studied.
the current PPI data on SSU processomes is very limited and the majority of the PPIs remain to be discovered.
the SSU processosome is a highly interconnected complex, and the current PPI data are sparse, with the LC dataset providing the most comprehensive coverage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
while the SSU processosome has been extensively studied, there is still a great deal of work to do.
the SSU processomes of different organisms have a core set of proteins that are highly conserved, but the protein-protein interaction networks are not.
the current PPI datasets for the SSU processomes from yeast and other organisms are not sufficient to build a comprehensive PPI map of the processomes.
